CALLER_STABLE_PATH_CREATE_RECOVERY.reason: A deterministic path can be chosen before mutation. A replayed create of an already-existing path fails rather than silently creating a second object, after which exact GET can verify the embedded op_id and intent and adopt the existing file. This is a create/readback recovery pattern, not proof of ownership if an unrelated actor could have written indistinguishable bytes.

BLOB_SHA_CURRENT_VALUE_CAS.reason: When current bytes differed, update_file with the old blob sha failed 409; update with the exact current blob sha succeeded.

BLOB_SHA_HISTORICAL_FENCE.reason: After A -> B -> A, Git content addressing returned the original A blob sha. The original historical sha was then accepted as the update precondition. Therefore blob sha proves current byte identity, not that no intervening write occurred and not a monotonic generation.

CONTENTS_SHA_AS_EXECUTION_GENERATION.reason: A stale execution attempt can become admissible again if current content cycles back to the same bytes. Workflows that need historical fencing need a monotonic revision/generation or a server-side precondition over a history-bearing identity, not only the content blob.

cross_system_revision.etcd: This live GitHub ABA result strengthens the prior etcd fixture conclusion: per-key VERSION/content identity is weaker than a history-bearing MOD/CREATE revision for historical fencing.
cross_system_revision.mcp: A deterministic task/op_id plus current-value CAS can solve handle rediscovery and some duplicate creation races, but a history-bearing execution generation and effect-side fence are still required for stale attempt exclusion across takeover.
cross_system_revision.openhands: The fenced HEAD marker candidate intentionally includes a monotonic base persistence_generation in addition to event digest/content identity, precisely to avoid treating identical content as a historical write fence.
